source_caption:
Set across post-war Poland and 1950s Paris, Cold War follows Wiktor, a musician, and Zula, a singer, whose intense relationship keeps pulling them together and tearing them apart. Their love story unfolds across borders, political pressure, different countries and years of separation, with music becoming the one thing that constantly connects them. The story was also inspired by director Paweł Pawlikowski’s own parents and their complicated relationship. (The Criterion Collection)

Shot in striking black and white and 4:3 by cinematographer Łukasz Żal, the film feels intimate even as it moves through years and different parts of Europe. Its short 84-minute runtime leaves a lot unsaid, letting the music, performances and images carry much of the emotion. Pawlikowski won Best Director at Cannes for the film, which also received three Oscar nominations, including Best Director, Best Foreign Language Film and Best Cinematography. (Festival de Cannes)

🎥: Cold War (2018)
Dir. Paweł Pawlikowski

source_details.synopsis: Cold War (Polish: Zimna wojna [ʑimna vojna]) is a 2018 historical romantic drama film directed by Paweł Pawlikowski, who co-wrote the screenplay with Janusz Głowacki and Piotr Borkowski. It is an international co-production by producers in Poland, France and the United Kingdom. Set in Poland and France during the Cold War from the late 1940s until the 1960s, the story follows a musical director (Tomasz Kot) who discovers a young singer (Joanna Kulig), exploring their subsequent love story over the years.
